research.ancient_remnants.hunter_monolit: A floating Monolith, revered by the hunting tribes of the scorching deserts. It granted them the agility and precision they needed to survive in lands where game was scarce and elusive, where feeding an entire settlement was no easy task.
research.ancient_remnants.warrior_monoli: The legendary Monolith of warriors, said to have multiplied the strength of countless heroes. It is mentioned in many myths and legends of our world. Its power is a great responsibility, and those who wield it must understand the burden they carry.
research.ancient_remnants.sentinel_monol: The Monolith of guardians was revered by monks who favored defense over aggression. It granted endurance and resilience, its blessing ideal for those who chose a secluded life, far from pointless battles and endless conflict.
research.ancient_remnants.cherry_monumen: Legend says the Monument of life was gifted to the world by a pair of divine twins. Beneath it flow springs of life and eternal youth, feeding the roots of ancient cherry trees that bloom throughout the year. Its energy heals both body and mind.
research.ancient_remnants.oakwood_monume: The Forest Monument is mentioned in elven manuscripts. Its blessing allowed forest peoples to preserve their lands while making better use of their scarce resources. The Monument’s gift increased the fertility of both soil and livestock.
research.ancient_remnants.coniferous_mon: The Coniferous Monument may be the only temple built jointly by the taiga and mountain dwarves. It blessed its followers with skill in architecture and mining. Yet its origins remain a mystery; perhaps the dwarves raised it with divine intervention.

config.ancient_remnants.option.placement: Spacing is the size of each structure placement region, measured in chunks. A new structure position is generated once per spacing × spacing region. Larger values result in fewer structures and greater distances between them.
Separation reduces the range of possible positions within each spacing region by this many chunks along each axis. Higher values move structures toward the beginning of each region.
